context.rework_reason: ORCH caught a factual error in §0 of lib/letflow/design/req206-swiftroute-scenario-execution.md: the design claimed 'No docs/issues/ISS-0388.yaml record exists in this repo, and no handoff shows an ls/find against R-Co succeeding', concluding REQ-205's company/org/process fixtures were still self-authored synthetic data. This was factually wrong and independently verifiable on this branch.

result.summary: Verified independently this session before correcting anything: (1) docs/issues/ISS-0388.yaml exists on this branch (was on main before this feature branch was cut); its status is 'resolved' and its resolution field states the fix landed in commit f7ffbeb6 / PR #766 (merged), replacing all 12 test/fixtures/simulation/{swiftroute,vortex,meridian}/ files with real R-Co-ported content -- real display_names, real actor_ids (7 swiftroute, 9 vortex, 10 meridian), real process graphs -- with zero Seed/Runner code changes needed. (2) `git log -1 --format='%an <%ae>%n%s' f7ffbeb6` confirms the commit is authored by Vladimir Titenko <tvolodi@gmail.com> -- the human user's own git identity ('tvolo' matches the literal R-Co filesystem path c:\Users\tvolo\dev\ai-dala\R-Co\ cited throughout this project), not any Claude (letflow-workspace) agent identity -- a genuinely different signal from a sandboxed agent fabricating provenance. (3) `git show f7ffbeb6 --stat` plus reading test/fixtures/simulation/swiftroute/org_structure.yaml directly confirms the specific falsifiable claim: swiftroute now has exactly 7 real-looking people (actor-swiftroute-{alice,marco,lena,tobias,jan,petra,hans}) under 4 groups, matching both the commit message's and ISS-0388's resolution field's '7 swiftroute, 9 vortex, 10 meridian' counts -- not a 2-person synthetic stub. Corrected §0 of the design to state the evidence chain above and reverse the prior conclusion: REQ-205's company/org/process fixtures ARE now real R-Co-ported content (fixed post-hoc by ISS-0388, a follow-up issue REQ-205's own RELEASE-VALIDATOR filed), not still synthetic. What did NOT change: the design's ultimate decision for THIS requirement's scope stands -- the 4 SwiftRoute *scenario* YAML files under tests/simulation/scenarios/ (a different file set from the company/org/process fixtures) remain independently verified unreachable from this sandbox (re-ran the same ls/find commands, same result), so REQ-206 still authors self-authored, structurally-faithful synthetic scenario content, clearly disclosed via header comments, mirroring REQ-205's original (now-superseded-for-those-files) precedent. Checked all other sections referencing 'synthetic'/'ISS-0388'/'byte-for-byte' (§1.1 scenario file layout, §1.3 parser rationale, §5 OQ-1/OQ-3 on org_structure.yaml actors) -- none depended on the now-corrected premise; actor ids used throughout the design (e.g. actor-swiftroute-marco, actor-swiftroute-alice) already match the real fixture's actual actor_ids, so no further changes needed there. Added a new recommendation in §0: file a follow-up issue mirroring ISS-0388's exact shape (discovered_by: RELEASE-VALIDATOR, tags: [fixture-porting, needs-r-co-access, s7], affected_files listing the 4 scenario YAMLs, related: [REQ-206]) for ORCH to file at Step 6/Step Final, so a future session/host with genuine R-Co access can later port the real tests/simulation/scenarios/*.yaml content, the same way ISS-0388 got REQ-205's fixtures fixed. No implementation code added or removed; the Runner extension shape, per-scenario execution plan, finding-reporting mechanism, and existing open questions are unchanged.
